note: CR-25.6: category composite scores that can be selected like any other score. A category is only offered when at least two benchmarks in it are on a 0-100-style, higher-is-better scale AND are measured for at least 60 % of the featured model families (measured with ops/ux-2026-09-12/bin/cr-25-6-coverage.mjs). The anchor set is fixed here, not derived per model: a model gets the category score only when it has a result on EVERY anchor, so two models' category scores are always an average over the same benchmarks. Where a benchmark exists in several versions, the build picks the newest version (Terminal-Bench v4.0 over v2.1; newestRow in lib/category-scores.mjs), never a retired version that happens to cover more models; within one version the wider row wins (CR-65.16: this note said 'widest coverage' until 17 Sep). Reasoning and Vision have only one qualifying benchmark each (Humanity's Last Exam, MMMU Pro) and therefore get no category score. 2026-09-16 (CR-38.2/38.3, F-98): anchors are weighted, not averaged flat — a benchmark whose top five independently measured results average at least 90 % of its ceiling counts at half weight (SATURATED_WEIGHT in lib/benchmark-matrix.mjs), because it no longer separates the best models. Today that applies to GPQA Diamond in Science, so cat_science is (CritPt + 0.5 x GPQA Diamond) / 1.5. A preference or judge score may not be an anchor at all: computeCategoryScores throws rather than silently redefining a published score if one is ever reclassified (assertNoJudgedAnchors).
